verdict.summary: A Development Mode app works in minutes, but since February 2026 it needs a Premium owner, is capped at 5 allowlisted users, gets a reduced endpoint set and is meant for non-commercial use. Opening to any user needs Extended Quota Mode, which Spotify grants only to established businesses with at least 250k MAU, after a partner application and a review of up to six weeks.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create an app in the dashboard, add a 127.0.0.1 or HTTPS redirect URI, and allowlist yourself. Assumes the owner already has Spotify Premium.

timeToProd.assumes: Extended Quota Mode so any Spotify user can connect; the only faster path is Development Mode, capped at 5 allowlisted users and non-commercial use.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Reaching 250k MAU as a registered business, Partner Application approval, then a quota extension review that 'can take up to six weeks'.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The six-week maximum and 250k MAU bar are sourced. How long it takes to reach 250k MAU while capped at 5 users is unknowable, so the range is a floor-style estimate.

verdict.cost: Development Mode requires the app owner to keep an active Spotify Premium subscription.

prerequisites.item: Spotify Premium on the app owner's account
prerequisites.why: Development Mode apps stop working if the owner's Premium lapses, and resume when they resubscribe.

prerequisites.item: HTTPS redirect URI, or a loopback IP literal (http://127.0.0.1:PORT) for local dev
prerequisites.why: localhost is not allowed as a redirect URI; validation has applied to new apps since 9 April 2025.

prerequisites.item: For Extended Quota: a legally registered business, a launched service and at least 250k MAU in key Spotify markets
prerequisites.why: Spotify only accepts extension applications from organizations, not individuals (since 15 May 2025).

prerequisites.item: A use case compatible with the Developer Policy
prerequisites.why: The policy bars training or ingesting Spotify content into ML/AI models and voice assistants that control Spotify.

scopeTiers.impact: All scopes are usable, but only for up to 5 allowlisted users per app, with a reduced endpoint set (no batch fetches, no other users' profiles/playlists, search limit 10) and quota shared across up to 25 Client IDs per developer.
Same 5-user cap. Library writes now go through PUT/DELETE /me/library with Spotify URIs in Development Mode. Voice-controlled assistants are prohibited by policy.
Any Spotify user can authorize, full endpoint set and a much higher rate limit, but only for the use case Spotify reviewed.

steps.title: Make sure the owner account has Premium
steps.detail: Development Mode requires an active Premium subscription on the app owner's account.

steps.title: Create an app in the dashboard
steps.detail: Log in to the developer dashboard, create an app, select Web API, and accept the Developer Terms. Up to 25 Development Mode Client IDs per developer since July 2026.

steps.title: Register redirect URIs
steps.detail: Generate HTTPS production URIs and http://127.0.0.1:PORT (or [::1]) for local dev; localhost is rejected.

steps.title: Allowlist test users
steps.detail: App > Settings > Users Management > Add new user (name + Spotify email). Up to 5 users; others can log in but get 403s.

steps.title: Implement Authorization Code (with PKCE if public client)
steps.detail: Authorize at https://accounts.spotify.com/authorize, exchange at https://accounts.spotify.com/api/token, store refresh tokens and re-authorize users before the 6-month refresh token lifetime ends.

steps.title: Build against the Development Mode endpoint set
steps.detail: Use /me, /me/playlists, /me/library and /playlists/{id}/items; avoid removed batch, browse, top-tracks and other-user endpoints; handle 429 with Retry-After and reason QUOTA_EXCEEDED.

steps.title: Check the use case against the Developer Policy
steps.detail: Confirm the agent doesn't ingest Spotify content into ML/AI models, profile users, or act as a voice assistant; draft data-minimization and deletion handling.

steps.title: Submit the Partner Application
steps.detail: Once you meet the business and 250k MAU criteria, submit the Partner Application from a company email via the form linked on the quota modes page.

steps.title: Submit the quota extension request
steps.detail: After partner approval: app Settings > Quota extension Request, complete the four-step questionnaire describing the use case, then Submit (status shows 'Sent').

steps.title: Wait for Spotify's review
steps.detail: Spotify says review can take up to six weeks and makes no guarantee of approval.

agentCanDo: Implement Authorization Code / PKCE with loopback and HTTPS redirect URIs
Refactor calls to the Development Mode endpoint set (/me/library, /playlists/{id}/items)
Check the use case against the Developer Policy's AI/ML and voice rules
Draft the quota extension questionnaire answers
humanMustDo: Keep Spotify Premium active on the owner account
Create the app and accept the Developer Terms in the dashboard
Add up to 5 users in Users Management
Submit the Partner Application and quota extension request as a registered business

blockers.symptom: A user logs in fine but every API call returns 403
blockers.cause: The user isn't on the app's Development Mode allowlist (max 5).
blockers.fix: Add them in Users Management, or get Extended Quota Mode.

blockers.symptom: The whole app suddenly stops working
blockers.cause: The owner's Spotify Premium subscription lapsed.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error returned is not documented.

blockers.fix: Use http://127.0.0.1:3000/callback or an HTTPS URI.

blockers.symptom: GET /tracks?ids=..., /browse/new-releases or /users/{id}/playlists fail, and search returns at most 10 results
blockers.cause: February 2026 Development Mode restrictions removed these endpoints and cut the search limit.
blockers.fix: Fetch items individually and use /me endpoints; Extended Quota apps keep the old behaviour.

blockers.cause: Development Mode quota is counted per developer account and shared across all your Client IDs.
blockers.fix: Cut call volume, cache metadata, or apply for Extended Quota.

blockers.symptom: Refresh returns invalid_grant about six months after a user connected
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens last 6 months from authorization, and refreshing doesn't extend them.
blockers.fix: Prompt the user to re-authorize before expiry.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error string is our assumption.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 1 hour; refresh tokens last 6 months from the original authorization and a refresh response may not include a new refresh token.
Rate limits use a rolling 30-second window and are much higher in Extended Quota Mode; Spotify publishes no exact numbers.
The Developer Policy says not to use the platform or content to train an ML/AI model or otherwise ingest Spotify content into one, which matters for LLM agents that pass track data to a model.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Whether sending metadata to an LLM at inference time counts as 'ingesting' is not clarified; treat as a legal question.

nuances.text: Development Mode is for learning and non-commercial personal projects and 'should not be relied on as a foundation for building or scaling a business'.
Development Mode user objects no longer include email, country or product, even with user-read-email.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The changes page lists these User fields as removed; it doesn't spell out whether Extended Quota apps keep them, but the migration guide says those apps need no migration.

nuances.text: Extended quota is granted for the use case Spotify reviewed only; new use cases need a new request.
